price_basis: USD Ellicott & Co. (the shop's own site)
one_line: The shop's own label: "We build collections of timeless heritage goods in collaboration with makers from around the world."
note: Reject: house label, sold only through the shop (tee, letterpress posters, recipe cards, grooming, decor). Not a separate house. Price is the shop's own, so it could not seat anyway. Ellicott's own site is its only channel found.

one_line: Stuarts London's page says it began as a small independent project making heritage-inspired menswear and everyday basics (retailer wording, not the brand's own).
source: https://wittmore.com/products/power-goods-black-super-weight-t-shirt; https://www.stuartslondon.com/en-au/collections/power-goods; https://powergoods.com (parked domain for sale, via MAXdomains); https://powergoods.co.uk (did not load, not read)
note: Bench: real brand carried by many retailers (Wittmore, Stuarts London, Blacksmith, Clark Street Mercantile and others) but I found no brand-owned site, so there is no first-party store or first-party price. Only prices are retailers' (USD $75 at Wittmore; AUD $62 for a tee at Stuarts London). Origin from Wittmore ('HQ and design is based in London, UK'); tee made in India; founding year from Stuarts London only. I could not open Ellicott's own Power Goods product page, so the namesake check against the shop's product is NOT done. Would change it: a brand-owned site with prices.

origin_city: Santa Barbara, CA (flagship city; site says only 'California')
one_line: Launched in California in 1964 as the "Original Casual Sneaker", disappeared in 1972 and was relaunched by its founder in 2008.
note: Footwear. Core shoe is my pick from the men's best sellers; Tiburon Trekker $165 and Maslon Desert Boot $160 sit nearby. The Santa Barbara flagship is the only store on the locator page. Product (sneakers, slip-ons, boots) matches the shop's category.

one_line: "Soft Goods is a Detroit garment factory built on grit and persistent craftsmanship."
note: Site confirmed by Sebastian. Factory founded 2017 by Josh York in Corktown; sold private-label for others first and opened its own web shop in 2025 (its own account). No own retail store or locator found; I could not read the stockists page. Heavyweight Tee $88. Also appears on American Trench's stockist list (Detroit) and made a collab tee with TOPO Designs ($69).

own_store: 4 (Denver Flagship, Fort Collins, Denver Base Camp, Hayes Valley San Francisco) https://topodesigns.com/pages/our-retail-stores
one_line: Founded on the belief that everyone experiences the outdoors differently, making durable, functional, classic outdoor gear.
note: Contradicts the brief: its own locator lists four stores, not two. The Denver flagship opened Nov 2013. Judgement call: it is an outdoor packs-and-apparel house rather than menswear; seated because it has a men's tee line, own stores and own prices, but Sebastian may want to bench it for category. At Ellicott it sits in Bags rather than Apparel.

one_line: "We believe great shoes should do more than look good — they should feel good to make, wear, and stand behind."
note: Footwear. Nisolo's own site gives no origin city or year; Nashville and 2011 come from two press pieces (one says 2011 is when the idea came). Entrepreneur mentions a Nashville brick-and-mortar store but nisolo.com has no store locator, so own_store is NONE, unconfirmed. Made in Peru and Mexico. Site was running a Friends & Family 30% banner; I used the regular price. Medium confidence on founding.

origin_city: Wigston Magna, Leicestershire (founding; design now Bristol)
note: A UK house (Thomas Glover, hand-frame knitter), not the American namesake. Knitwear factory in Manchester, other items made across the UK, Spain and Portugal. Own site lists no stores; trade press mentions a Selfridges space and pop-ups, which I did not count as own stores. I did not check that the Ellicott product is this Peregrine (shop sells knitwear/outerwear).

one_line: A Philadelphia-based brand founded to bring forward the exceptional manufacturing that exists in the United States.
note: Founding year 2012 is from FashionUnited, not the brand's own site. Own stockists page lists Ellicott & Co., Franklin & Poe and Weitzenkorns (confirmed) but NOT Vestis and NOT an Ardmore store; I did not check the Imogene + Willie page. No own stores. Also sells coats ($925 trench) and Interlock Long Sleeve Tee $110.

one_line: A small line of functional, distinctively West Coast outerwear, begun by Erik Prowell from t-shirts made in his garage.
note: Has men's and women's lines. Stores: Portland (1029 SW Harvey Milk St) and Bend (916 NW Wall St, opened July). The LA store opened in 2017 is no longer on the stores page. 2010 is when its own story says the brand launched; tee line began 2009.

one_line: "Making naturally fitting footwear that allows your feet the freedom to be just as nature intended."
note: Footwear. Founder Andrew Rademacher; first product, the Primal, released September 2011; company moved to Boulder in January 2016, so the original home city is NC. Store locator is a retailer finder (Locally), not an own-store list, so NONE. Core shoe is my pick (Boulder Boot $155); Summit Pro Boot $230. Prices for Primal Zen not read.
